blocks.text: Buying a Farm or Agricultural Property in Maple Ridge, BC

parts.t: Agricultural real estate in the City of Maple Ridge spans productive lowland peat and alluvial soils in Northwest Maple Ridge along the Pitt and Alouette rivers, benchland hobby farms and horse properties in Websters Corners and Northeast Maple Ridge, and rural agricultural parcels in Whonnock and South Albion.

Under Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 (Part 5 Agricultural Zones, consolidated to July 28, 2026), farm parcels are classified into five specific zones: A-1 Small Holding Agricultural (min. lot 2 ha / 4.9 acres), A-2 Upland Agricultural (min. lot 4 ha / 9.9 acres), A-3 Extensive Agricultural (min. lot 8 ha / 19.8 acres), A-4 Intensive Greenhouse (min. lot 1.8 ha / 4.4 acres), and A-5 Agricultural Only (min. lot 8 ha / 19.8 acres, where residential is not a principal use).

blocks.text: ALR House-Size Rules, Farm Classification (BC Assessment) & Water Rights

parts.t: Most Maple Ridge farm listings sit inside the provincial Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) administered by the Agricultural Land Commission (ALC). Under ALC regulations and Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, buyers must verify principal residence floor-area caps, small secondary residence rules, BC Assessment 'Farm Class' income thresholds (which significantly reduce annual property taxes and can exempt qualifying buyers from GST on farmland), surface or groundwater irrigation licences, and floodplain construction elevations.

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Maple Ridge Farms and Agricultural Land for Sale

parts.t: What are the agricultural zones in Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019?

Maple Ridge has five agricultural zones: A-1 Small Holding Agricultural (min. 2 ha / 4.9 ac), A-2 Upland Agricultural (min. 4 ha / 9.9 ac), A-3 Extensive Agricultural (min. 8 ha / 19.8 ac), A-4 Intensive Greenhouse (min. 1.8 ha / 4.4 ac), and A-5 Agricultural Only (min. 8 ha / 19.8 ac, where residential use is not permitted as a principal use). How do I qualify for BC Assessment Farm Class tax status in Maple Ridge?

To maintain BC Assessment Farm Class status, the property must generate qualifying gross annual agricultural income based on parcel size: $10,000 for parcels under 0.8 hectares (1.98 acres), $2,500 for parcels between 0.8 ha and 4.0 ha (1.98 to 9.88 acres), and $2,500 plus 5% of the actual land value above 4.0 ha for larger farms.
Can I build a second house on an ALR farm in Maple Ridge?

Under provincial Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) rules and Maple Ridge Bylaw No. 7600-2019, a small secondary residence (typically up to 90 sq m / 968 sq ft on parcels under 40 ha, subject to municipal siting, servicing, and floodplain permits) may be permitted in addition to the principal residence.
Are commercial kennels allowed on Maple Ridge agricultural land?

Under Section 501 of Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, a commercial kennel in the A-1 zone is permitted only on parcels of 4.0 hectares (9.9 acres) or larger and must meet specific setback and noise regulations.
Does GST apply when buying a farm or hobby farm in Maple Ridge?

Used residential housing is generally exempt from GST, while commercial farmland or acreage exceeding the residential curtilage can be subject to 5% GST unless the buyer is a GST registrant acquiring the farm for commercial agricultural use.
